adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Capacity planning memo for the matching engine

Over the last two quarters the exchange has grown from twelve to forty venues, and the operations team has asked us to explain why the latency budget keeps slipping during the opening auction. This memo summarizes the measurements we collected between January and March, describes the changes we made to the deployment, and lists the questions we still cannot answer.

We instrumented every gateway node with the same tracing library and sampled one request in twenty, which produced roughly ninety million spans per day. After filtering out health checks and synthetic probes, about four fifths of the remaining traffic consisted of limit orders, while cancellations and amendments made up the rest. The busiest hour was always the first hour after the open, when order rates rose by a factor of six and queue depths along the ingest path grew faster than the autoscaler could react. We added two extra partitions to the inbound topic in February and moved the matching workers onto dedicated hosts, which removed most of the noisy-neighbor complaints from the support queue.

The graphical front end also deserves a note. Traders reported that the blotter refreshed slowly whenever they switched between accounts, and after some digging we found that each account switch rebuilt the entire position table from scratch. Caching the table per session, keyed on the account identifier, removed almost all of that redundant work. We shipped the change behind a flag on the fourteenth and rolled it out to all desks by the end of the month. No incidents were attributed to the rollout, although two desks asked for the old behavior back during the first week and were told to wait for the next release.

Support tickets told a similar story. Most weeks the queue stayed empty, but the two days after each release brought a burst of questions about the new screens, and the team answered them from a shared document that slowly drifted out of date. We have since moved that document into the repository and asked the release manager to review it before every deployment, which has cut the number of repeated questions by roughly half.

On the storage side, the archive team migrated the historical trade repository to a columnar format and reported a fourfold reduction in disk usage. The migration spanned three scheduled maintenance windows, mostly because the verification jobs had to re-read every partition and compare checksums against the original files. Restoring a single day of history is now far cheaper for the compliance group, which says the change will make their quarterly audits considerably less painful.

Our profiling shows that matching a batch of n resting orders costs O(n log n) comparisons on average, and the worst case remains O(n^2) when the book is heavily skewed toward one side.

We recommend funding one more engineer for the next two quarters and repeating this review after the summer hardware refresh.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Minutes of the Riverside planning committee, third session

The chair opened the meeting at seven and reminded members that the developer's revised drawings had been circulated on Friday, along with a letter from the residents' association and a summary of the drainage study. Six members were present, one seat was empty, and the recording secretary took notes for the file.

Mr. Alvarez presented the revised plan for the former warehouse site. The proposal now includes forty-two apartments, a small grocery on the ground floor, and a courtyard that opens onto Mill Street. The applicant has agreed to widen the sidewalk along the north edge and to plant eleven trees, though the species has not been settled. Several members asked about parking, and the applicant's engineer explained that the garage would hold fifty cars, with bicycle racks beside the loading bay.

Ms. Chen, speaking for the residents' association, said the neighborhood supported the housing but objected to the height of the eastern wing. She noted that the afternoon sun would be blocked from the community garden, that the windows of the townhouses on Alder Lane would look straight into the new stairwell, and that the delivery trucks would arrive before the school buses. The applicant offered to lower the eastern wing by one story and to move the loading bay to the rear, subject to a review by the fire marshal, who has not yet responded to the revised drawings.

A lengthy discussion followed about the drainage study. The consultant explained that the site sits on clay, that the existing culvert is undersized, and that a detention pond would be needed at the southern corner. The cost of the pond, she estimated, would fall on the developer, although the maintenance agreement would bind the city for twenty years. Mr. Okafor asked whether the pond could double as a playground, and the consultant said the slope made that impractical. The committee asked for a written opinion before the next session.

Two members asked about the timeline for the traffic study, which the city's consultant has promised for the end of the quarter. The chair said the study would be paid from the ward's discretionary fund, that the results would be posted on the committee's page, and that residents would have thirty days to comment. Ms. Chen asked whether the comment period could be extended through the holidays, and the chair agreed to consider it.

The meeting returned to the matter of the trees. Ms. Chen's association had collected signatures in favor of preserving the two mature oaks near the entrance, and the applicant's landscape architect confirmed that both could be kept if the driveway were shifted six feet to the east. That shift, however, would affect the property line and require a variance. The committee voted five to one to request the variance application and to postpone the final decision until the surveyor's report arrives.

Before adjourning, the chair read a short statement thanking the clerk for her work during the budget season, and the members agreed to meet again on the second Tuesday of next month.
